title: TDD
lede: How a feature gets built one thin slice at a time: a failing test, the least code that passes it, a quality check, a commit.

slices.name: Plan the slices
slices.role: Split the PRD into vertical slices and confirm their size once with the user.
details: If plan.md is missing, the agent writes it from prd.md first.

details.t: Each slice cuts through every layer
more: Data, logic, UI and tests together.
After the size is confirmed, slices run without pausing.

prep.name: Before code
prep.role: For each slice, decide the interface and list the behaviors to test.

details.t: Name the assumption the slice tests
more: Use the design's evidence, or mark it unknown.
If a probe contradicts the intent, revise the design, PRD and unfinished slices first.

qs: Why list behaviors to test instead of implementation steps?

loop.name: Red, then green
loop.role: Write one failing test, then the least code that makes it pass, and repeat.
details: The first test is a tracer bullet: one behavior, proving the path works end to end.
Tests use the public interface only, so they survive an internal refactor.
risks: Writing all tests first verifies imagined behavior; one test at a time keeps them honest.
A test that fails for a different reason, or an old test that breaks, stops the loop for /investigate.
qs: What goes wrong if you write all the tests before any code?

refactor.name: Refactor check
refactor.role: Score each touched file on the four-part rubric and audit the tests before committing.

more: A fix under 30 lines is applied in place, then re-tested and re-scored.
A bigger fix is surfaced to the user, never silently patched.
Assertions use sentinel values, not defaults.
Every form of a new flag is covered.
At least one test is written from the caller's side.

commit.name: Commit and log
commit.role: Commit the red, green and refactor steps, log the slice, then start the next one.
details: Commits: test (red), feat (green), and refactor only if something was refactored.
Each slice's status is appended to tdd-log.md.

done.name: All slices pass
done.role: Run the full suite, then /code-refiner, then stop for the user's review.
details: /code-refiner runs in auto-fix mode: correctness and structure reviews, then one fix pass.
A summary lists what was built, the tests and any deviation from the plan.

slice.d: A thin piece of a feature that cuts through every layer and works on its own.

rubric.d: Four scores for code: Quality, Readability, Encapsulation, Clarity.

sentinel.d: A non-default test value, so a bug that silently resets a field can't hide.

tracer.d: The first test, which proves the path works end to end.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand how scaffold's /tdd skill builds a feature test-first, one slice at a time.
